docs.title: Calories, BMR and TDEE
docs.content: Daily calorie targets should start from BMR (Mifflin-St Jeor) then TDEE = BMR x activity factor. Muscle gain usually uses TDEE + 200-300 kcal. Fat loss usually uses TDEE - 300-500 kcal. Maintenance stays near TDEE. Extreme deficits harm training. Floor calories: about 1600 kcal for most men and 1400 kcal for most women unless a clinician directs otherwise.

docs.title: Protein targets
docs.content: A practical evidence-based range is 1.6-2.2 g of protein per kg for muscle gain, and 2.0-2.4 g/kg during fat loss. Spread protein across 3-5 meals. Vegetarian sources include paneer, dal, curd, tofu, soya, whey, and eggs if eggetarian.

docs.title: Missed workouts
docs.content: Do not double tomorrow's session after a missed workout. Shift the remaining week forward by one day or skip the least important accessory day. Protect rest.

docs.title: Chest exercise substitutions
docs.content: Barbell bench press can be replaced with dumbbell bench press, machine chest press, or weighted push-ups. Dumbbells are usually the closest hypertrophy substitute.

docs.title: Vegetarian protein swaps
docs.content: Paneer can be swapped for tofu, Greek yogurt/curd, soya chunks, or extra dal plus a protein shake while watching daily protein.

docs.title: Choosing a training split
docs.content: Beginners on 2-3 days should use full body. Four days is usually upper/lower. Intermediate 3-day is Push/Pull/Legs. Do not pick PPL only because the goal is muscle gain.

docs.title: Progressive overload
docs.content: Add load or reps when you hit the top of the rep range with good form. Example: 40 kg x 8 -> 40 kg x 10 -> 42.5 kg x 8.

docs.title: Recovery, sleep and stress
docs.content: Aim for 7-9 hours of sleep. High stress and poor sleep are reasons to keep calories closer to maintenance and reduce extra isolation volume.

docs.title: Indian gym diet patterns
docs.content: A high-protein Indian template: breakfast oats or idli/dosa + sambar or eggs/curd; lunch rice or roti + dal + sabzi + paneer/tofu/chicken; snack curd or whey; dinner roti + protein + vegetables.

docs.title: Safety and medical limits
docs.content: Sharp joint pain is a stop signal. Extreme calorie targets, purging, or crash dieting are not valid fitness strategies. Eating-disorder symptoms and medical conditions need a qualified clinician.

docs.title: Supplements
docs.content: Food first. Best-supported gym supplements are creatine monohydrate 3-5 g daily and protein powder if food protein is low. This is not medical advice.

docs.title: Hydration
docs.content: About 30-35 ml of water per kg of body weight, plus extra on training days. Pale straw urine is a practical check.
